evidence.excerpt: An external contract can take over control flow and call back before the first function invocation finishes. Remediation: perform internal state changes before the external call, using checks-effects-interactions, or use a reentrancy lock. A lock blocks the unwanted callback into the protected path; it does not prevent control passing to the external callee.

Low-level calls return a success value. A low-level call may fail and return false while the caller continues. Ignoring that return value can leave contract accounting inconsistent because the caller may record an operation as successful when the call failed.

Missing access restrictions on functions that transfer ether can allow arbitrary users to withdraw funds. Implement controls so withdrawals can only be triggered by authorized parties. The source's sample access control checks msg.sender against a stored creator or owner and uses an onlyOwner modifier.

Price oracle manipulation exploits weaknesses in price feeds to distort contract logic; validate inputs and use resilient oracle sources.
Aggregate multiple price sources. Use time-weighted averages (TWAPs) over sufficient windows to resist short-lived manipulations. Reject prices older than a maximum staleness threshold.
